segments.he: הי' א' מאנ"ש שהי' קם בחצות כל לילה ומתייגע א"ע לומר כל תהלים והי' בא לו בקושי גדול עפי"כ הי' גומר כל תהלים כל לילה, והי' בשכונתו רב מכת המתנגדים ואמר הרב הנ"ל שאלו השני ברסלבר (היינו זה עם התהלים שלו ועוד אחד הי' מאנ"ש שהי' מתייגע ולומד כל יום קודם התפלה איזה דפים גמרא) לא מניחים אותו בשום אופן להיות מתנגד על ברסלבר כי נתפעל כ"כ מהם וכו'.
segments.en: Only at the end did a senior government official happen to encounter them, found favor in their eyes, and gave them counsel: it was known to him that the king was by nature compassionate — possessed of a mercy so great that even someone utterly guilty could, by appealing to this mercy, be forgiven entirely. Therefore they should write a petition to the emperor — not mentioning that they were innocent or had done no wrong, and not writing complaints. On the contrary: they should write that in truth they admit they had sinned — but not with intent to defy the king's authority. And they had already received punishment — sitting so many years in prison and being beaten — and they were old and weak. And knowing that the king possesses such mercy that even one entirely guilty by strict law can be forgiven — therefore they beseech his mercy. And so they did. And immediately a decree came to release them entirely.
